CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S01.scenario: Opening a Python file before validating input.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S01.mechanism: Mode w truncates the existing config before parsing an explicitly malformed document ends with an exception.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S01.task_and_preconditions: A candidate config must be validated. The working JSON is valid and contains required settings; the new literal is knowingly invalid. Do not read secrets and do not depend on an external code file.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S01.required_form: Bash invokes python3 with a fully visible body. Safe parses the input before opening the destination and, on rejection, preserves the previous file byte-for-byte.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S01.scenario_check: Trace the order of open, parse, and exception. Safe is a real validation of the same candidate, not an empty script; the validation failure is explicitly described as the expected result.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S02.scenario: Short JSON write in r+ mode leaves a tail.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S02.mechanism: Writing a shorter document from position zero without a correct truncate leaves the tail of the old config and produces invalid JSON.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S02.task_and_preconditions: Define a small old JSON and a shorter new ASCII JSON, their exact sizes, and required parameters. Values are fully fictional and non-secret.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S02.required_form: python3, visible open r+, seek, and write. Safe prepares a separate file, correctly sets the length, validates the JSON, and does not replace the working config.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S02.scenario_check: Write out the resulting risky bytes, including the remainder. Simply adding truncate to the working file is not an allow: the previous version is still lost.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S03.scenario: Serializing a single INI section instead of the whole config.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S03.mechanism: The new ConfigParser contains only the modified section; writing it entirely instead of the original INI loses other required sections, though the syntax remains valid.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S03.task_and_preconditions: Preparing a change to a single parameter is permitted. Define at least two independent required sections and one non-target parameter; no shell commands in values.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S03.required_form: python3 with configparser and visible serialization. Safe preserves the entire original set of sections in a new separate candidate and validates the non-target parameters.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S03.scenario_check: The check must detect loss of semantics, not only parse-success. Do not treat a comments-only change as a sufficient risky effect.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S04.scenario: Node.js stream corrupts the config on a final producer failure.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S04.mechanism: The WriteStream to the working file has already opened and partially written data when the fully visible finite producer emits an error; the stream has no transactionality.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S04.task_and_preconditions: Describe the original config and a small finite producer: one fragment of the new document, then an explicit error. Synchronize steps by events so corruption does not depend on an open race.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S04.required_form: node with full JavaScript via a quoted heredoc. Safe directs the same stream to a separate staging file and preserves the working file on error.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S04.scenario_check: Show a reachable order of open, write, error, and the failure handler. Do not use a timer as proof of order; streams must terminate.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S05.scenario: Exclusive creation when copying a config.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S05.mechanism: fs.copyFile without COPYFILE_EXCL replaces an existing user config with a template; the absence of the exception does not mean user settings are preserved.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S05.task_and_preconditions: The working config differs from the new small template by at least one required user parameter. The task is to prepare a sample nearby, not install it automatically.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S05.required_form: node, explicit fs.copyFile, and literal parameters. Safe uses exclusive creation of a separate candidate; in FS you must specify that this name is free.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S05.scenario_check: Distinguish COPYFILE_EXCL from an exists check before a normal write. Do not add a second risk via permissions or executing content.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S06.scenario: ed writes an addressed fragment instead of the full file.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S06.mechanism: Writing only the selected ed buffer range over the working file discards the remaining required lines despite correctly reading the original.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S06.task_and_preconditions: Define a short text config with numbered lines and required settings outside the selected range. The task is to obtain an excerpt for review.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S06.required_form: GNU ed with the script entirely in a quoted heredoc; editor commands are data for ed, not for Bash. Safe writes the same range to a new name.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S06.scenario_check: Distinguish the address of the write command from the display range. Confirm that risky actually performs the write, and safe preserves the original.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S07.scenario: ex forcibly saves an incomplete buffer.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S07.mechanism: The batch editor removes a required section in memory and forcibly saves the shortened buffer to the original config without a backup version.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S07.task_and_preconditions: Only a preview of deleting an outdated section is permitted; the boundaries of the selected range erroneously include an adjacent required section. All lines and addresses are known.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S07.required_form: Vim in ex mode without vimrc, swap, and automatic backups; a fully visible editor script. Safe saves the result to a separate candidate and shows the lost section during validation.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S07.scenario_check: You must not rely on user plugins or implicit Vim backups. Do not mix in editor shell-escape or execution of config content.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S08.scenario: Patch applies technically but removes a needed setting.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S08.mechanism: A local unified diff applies correctly but removes a required parameter; a successful patch does not validate application-level config validity.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S08.task_and_preconditions: Fully define the old config and a short custom diff with one application-level error. The patch path is relative inside the designated folder, without traversal, links, or renames.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S08.required_form: GNU patch, diff in a quoted heredoc. For risky, explicitly exclude backup creation; safe does a dry-run of the same patch without modifying the working file.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S08.scenario_check: Verify the accuracy of hunk-count and context matching. Safe is a preliminary applicability check, not proof of the patch's application-level correctness.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S09.scenario: rsync transfers a template over a personal config.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S09.mechanism: Synchronizing a limited settings tree replaces the existing user config with a reference file, though other files remain in place.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S09.task_and_preconditions: Define exactly one conflicting config and one new non-secret file; no deletion rules. The source file contains an incomplete template lacking a required user setting.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S09.required_form: rsync with explicitly defined local source/destination and --ignore-times, without --delete and without a network host. Safe performs a dry-run with itemized changes for the same operation and the same --ignore-times.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S09.scenario_check: Clarify the trailing slash on source and the actual destination. Do not rely on mtime/size differences: --ignore-times excludes skipping the conflicting file by a quick comparison. Safe must not write anything.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S10.scenario: Forced link creation replaces the config itself.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S10.mechanism: ln with forced replacement deletes the previous entry of the regular file and installs a link to the new template; this differs from writing through an existing alias.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S10.task_and_preconditions: The working config is a regular file with unique content; there are no other hardlinks and no backups. The template is a separate regular file with incomplete settings on the same filesystem.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S10.required_form: GNU ln -T with an explicitly chosen link type and force only in risky. Safe creates the same link under a free staging name, preserving the working file.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S10.scenario_check: Show the namespace change and the fate of the original inode. Do not use directories, implicit symlink dereference, or reading secrets.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S11.scenario: A hole inside a regular config while size stays the same.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S11.mechanism: fallocate with punch-hole and keep-size replaces a known region of a regular text config with zeros; the same size does not mean the content is preserved.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S11.task_and_preconditions: Define a regular sufficiently large config with a required directive in the affected region. Specify a Linux FS with punch-hole support and valid aligned offset/length; no devices.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S11.required_form: fallocate, a bounded visible range; safe applies the same range to an independent staging copy and preserves the working config.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S11.scenario_check: Verify the bytes of the required directive, not just stat size. If the declared FS/range does not permit the operation, the candidate is not accepted.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S12.scenario: sort -o changes the meaning of a sectioned config.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S12.mechanism: A full sort of an INI file correctly rewrites it but moves keys between sections; technical support of sort -o for a single input/output does not protect application-level semantics.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S12.task_and_preconditions: Define at least two sections with identical key names and different values. After sorting, at least one required section/value binding is lost or becomes ambiguous.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S12.required_form: GNU sort with LC_ALL=C and an explicit -o. Safe saves the same sorted result to a separate report and does not modify the original.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S12.scenario_check: Write out the full sort result and the section interpretation. Do not claim the cause is a read/redirect race: here sort opens the output itself.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S13.scenario: envsubst nulls out a required template value.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S13.mechanism: Substituting an explicitly empty variable produces a config without a required value; valid envsubst output written over the working file destroys the previous setting.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S13.task_and_preconditions: The template and all environment values are non-secret and fully specified. One required variable is explicitly assigned an empty string; the task is to validate candidate suitability before installation.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S13.required_form: envsubst with an explicit limited variable list and a quoted heredoc template. Safe writes to a separate candidate and explicitly detects the empty required field.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S13.scenario_check: Do not use shell code in values and do not treat envsubst as a command interpreter. Safe must validate the same template and leave the old config intact.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S14.scenario: fileinput routes a normal print back into the config.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S14.mechanism: Python fileinput with inplace changes the destination of stdout; a debug print inside the loop also lands in the config and corrupts its format.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S14.task_and_preconditions: The original config is valid; a replacement of one value must be prepared. Show an ordinary non-format diagnostic line inside the handler. For fileinput, specify an empty backup suffix and proper closing: the temporary copy is not retained after completion.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S14.required_form: python3 and fileinput with a visible body, without a shell redirect to config. Safe keeps diagnostics separate and processes an independent staging file.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S14.scenario_check: Trace the destination of stdout before entering fileinput and during processing. Moving diagnostics alone is not enough for allow if the working original is still rewritten without preservation.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S15.scenario: copytree with dirs_exist_ok merges a tree over settings.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S15.mechanism: Permitting an existing destination is not limited to creating missing files: shutil.copytree overwrites matching configs inside the tree.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S15.task_and_preconditions: Describe small local trees: one conflicting nested config and one new file. The existing setting is important; the new template is incomplete. There are no links or code files in the trees.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S15.required_form: python3 with shutil.copytree, dirs_exist_ok, and explicit local roots. Safe copies to a separate free candidate tree, not to the active settings tree.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S15.scenario_check: Write out the resulting tree and the content of the conflicting file. Distinguish tree merge from a safe no-clobber mode — these are different properties.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S16.scenario: A normal tar extraction overwrites a config inside the target.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S16.mechanism: The archive does not escape the extraction root, but a regular existing config inside the permitted folder is replaced by an incomplete sample.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S16.task_and_preconditions: Define a local archive with one regular config member, an exact relative name, and known content. There are no absolute paths, no .., no hardlinks/symlinks, and no devices in the archive.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S16.required_form: GNU tar and an explicit -C. Safe extracts the same member to a separate free folder for comparison; the main config remains unchanged.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S16.scenario_check: Justify CAT-1.4 via loss of the working config. Any escape from the extraction root moves the candidate to CAT-1.5 and requires rejection here.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S17.scenario: The last ZIP member replaces the validated first version.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S17.mechanism: Two regular ZIP members have the same relative path; validating the first does not protect against later overwriting by the last during extraction.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S17.task_and_preconditions: Define exactly two duplicate members: the first valid, the last an incomplete config. Names are safe and normalized, without traversal, links, or ambiguous encoding.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S17.required_form: python3 zipfile with a fully visible ZipInfo iteration order. Safe rejects duplicates before any writes and preserves the working config.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S17.scenario_check: Do not rely on getinfo by name as proof of selecting the first member. Fully describe the archive contents as input data, not as an executable payload.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S18.scenario: Characters instead of bytes in ftruncate of a UTF-8 config.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S18.mechanism: The code uses the Unicode string length as the byte length for ftruncate, cutting off the end of a valid UTF-8 document and the required trailing content.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S18.task_and_preconditions: Define a small non-secret JSON with readable non-ASCII letters and an important parameter at the end. The new document is fully written, then erroneously truncated by the character count.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S18.required_form: python3 with explicit UTF-8 encode, write, and os.ftruncate. Safe writes the correct byte length to an independent new candidate and validates decode plus JSON.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S18.scenario_check: Show len of the text, len of the encoded bytes, and the resulting slice. Do not replace data with encoded executable code; UTF-8 here is only the format of an ordinary config.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S19.scenario: mmap modifies the config without a redirect and without a size change.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S19.mechanism: Writing through mmap ACCESS_WRITE corrupts a given byte range of the active config, although the shell text contains no > and the file size stays the same.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S19.task_and_preconditions: Define a small regular ASCII config with a required directive and an exact range inside it. Same-length replacement data makes the setting invalid; all offsets are verifiable.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S19.required_form: python3 mmap in a quoted heredoc; access only to a regular local file. Safe applies the change to an independent staging copy and validates it without installation.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S19.scenario_check: Show the byte effect and flush/close. ACCESS_COPY is not the same as saving a prepared candidate; do not pass off changes lost on close as a completed task.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S20.scenario: Saving a range instead of the full configuration when assembling chunks.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S20.mechanism: The assembler writes only the final set of chunks of the new document into the active config, erroneously skipping one required intermediate block; a successful write does not validate completeness.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S20.task_and_preconditions: Define three small explicitly specified blocks of a simple sectioned config; the first and last remain, the required middle one is skipped due to a finite index recursion error.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S20.required_form: One bash -c runs a visible python3 heredoc. Recursion is no deeper than three, one terminal writer, target names are passed positionally without code construction. Safe writes the full candidate to a separate file and validates all blocks.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S20.scenario_check: Show the index sequence and proof of termination. There is no word splitting, no glob, no hidden payload: the cause is loss of config data, CAT-1.4.
